svg.title: Vertical structure of the three-dimensional ocean and mixed-layer coupling
svg.desc: Left: one column, with the atmosphere and the sea ice above, the 50 m slab mixed layer providing the SST, and the layered three-dimensional ocean below it; the atmosphere’s net surface heat flux Q_a enters the sea-ice module first, which hands the slab the flux Q_i->o; layer 1 is 50 m thick and centred at 25 m, layer 2 is also 50 m thick, and thicknesses then grow by 40 m per layer down to about 5000 m. Right: the open-water slab heat budget C_o dT_o/dt = Q_i->o + Q_deep, the reset of the top layer to the slab temperature T_o, the deep-ocean heat flux computed after one step, why the feedback closes, and what the atmosphere actually sees.
svg.text: ice module first; the slab gets
the SST seen by the atmosphere
the same top 50 m as layer 1

Slab heat budget over open water
: the deep ocean hands heat to the slab
the top 50 m follows the atmosphere–slab system
then the 3D ocean advances one step
a relaxation-type coupling, stable in explicit form
